description: World runtime feel and presentation constants (docs/runtime/WORLD_RUNTIME.md). None of these is published by MeowDB: they are isometric-3D adaptation decisions, each with a reason. Read through WorldTuning; never duplicated in code.

ambient_neighbours.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.7.6: the presentation-only ambient layer for neighbouring hunting maps is milestone M3 and ships behind this flag; the World Review decides whether it stays on (open question 8). Not implemented (M3).

transition.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.5: a warp fades to black over 0.2 s and back over 0.2 s (whole warp <= 0.6 s); after the fade the player must be on the floor within 10 physics frames, and after 30 frames without floor the session re-places the player at player_spawns[0]. Gate commits blend camera bounds over 0.35 s; lighting/BGM crossfade over 0.5 s.

spawns.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.5 and 4.7.1: a realize queues monster spawns nearest-first, at most 8 per frame, each fading in over 0.3 s; spawn slots stand at least 1.2 m apart and at least 4 m from every portal arrival. A slot first tries to land on its spawn area's own tier (within 0.6 m of the area's surface height), then on any walkable top surface in the area. Every slot stays inside the map's mob region, the layout footprint inset by 2 m (section 4.7.4); a map with MeowDB spawns but no exported spawn area samples that whole region (every map exports areas today). The clearance probe is 0.35 m in radius and as tall as the species' body (its canonical sprite height x WorldScale.actor when monsters/<id>.json fits the model to the sprite height), never shorter than 0.8 m, the old proxy approximation. NPC interaction spaces (the brief's isometric spawn rules): a slot stands at least slot_npc_clearance_m (2.5 m) from every NPC of its map, the 1.6 m talk sphere (npc.interaction_radius_m) plus the widest touch-zone half-width (Orange Mushroom 63 px x 0.025 / 2 = 0.79 m), so no monster appears where a player stands to talk (Sam stood inside Snail Hunting Ground I's Snail_3 region, Mai 1.6 m from A Split Road's BlueSnail_6). Density: a spawn region takes a share of its species' slots by weight as before, but never more slots than leave min_area_per_slot_m2 (8 m^2, a patch about 2.8 m across, room for an Orange Mushroom's touch zone and a walk) each; the rest go to the species' other regions, and what none of them can hold spills, once every species has its own regions, to the least crowded region of the map, so one species' overflow never takes another species' room (Tomato Field had 5 Blue Snails in 16 m^2; 000001001 had 16 slots in 88 m^2). Counts and species never change, only where the slots stand. A respawn is never realized within respawn_player_clearance_m (2.0 m) of the player's feet: the Orange Mushroom's touch zone reaches 0.79 m (1.11 m at its corners) from its feet plus the 0.3 m player body, so 2 m leaves a margin; the slot's monster waits (still alive in MapInstanceState, so capacity and counts stay canonical) until the player has moved away. Classic MapleStory makes no such promise; the brief asks that spawns avoid appearing directly inside the player.

map_mob_rate.reason: MisoStory decision on a MeowDB conflict (Iteration Three spawns audit, docs/review/it3_audit.json 'spawns'). Every Maple Island map carries a MeowDB mob rate (0.6x on 000000030, 1.5x on 000000050, 1.3x on 000001000 and 000001001, 1.2x on 000001014, 1.0x elsewhere). MeowDB's mechanics pages say it is ignored: the spawn-engine guide (updated 2026-08-24) 'Other MapleStory servers multiplied map capacity by it. MSC does not. The live game ignores it; capacity comes only from spawn-point count and the player scalar', the glossary (2026-09-04) 'There is no separate map-wide multiplier', and /formulas/spawns 'Capacity = floor(SpawnPoints x PlayerScalar)'. MeowDB's map pages and the monster-page MOB RATE tooltip say it multiplies capacity ('expect about 63 monsters up at a time instead of 42', self-labelled 'our best reading from closed-beta play'), which also contradicts the same page's own player scalar and exceeds the spawn-point count. Neither reading touches respawn speed (every row shows ~7.5s at every rate). apply false keeps the mechanics pages' reading: capacity = floor(points x PlayerScalar). apply true multiplies that capacity by the map's canonical mob_rate, capped at the spawn-point count because the runtime keeps one monster per MeowDB spawn point (SpawnModel.capacity_for_map). The canonical formulas/spawn_rate.json keeps MeowDB's own statement (map_spawn_rate_multiplier.applied_by_msc) as data, not as this switch.

grounding.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.9 and 4.13 (L1): a point counts as grounded when a ray from 1 m above to 3 m below hits walkable collision first, and the grounded point is within 0.3 m of that surface; a 0.3 x 1.5 m capsule lifted 0.05 m must be clear of blocking and containment collision. The capsule approximates the player body for static checks; the controller owns the real one (data/misostory/movement.json). A blocking surface lying within 0.05 m above walkable ground counts as that ground (interior floors carry a coplanar Walls slab 3 mm above Ground; Heena stands in her bush hull). When an arrival point or player spawn is not grounded or its capsule is blocked (a door mound, a hedge, a gate hull), the nearest grounded, clear point inside the map and outside every trigger is searched on rings up to 5 m around it in 0.5 m steps, inward first, and the move is logged as a warning (a Blender fix is the real cure).

containment.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.6: every map is walled by an invisible ring on the containment layer at footprint + 1.0 m (just outside the 1 m terrain overhang AUTHORING.md allows). The spec's '4 m tall' assumes flat maps; terraces rise up to ~10 m above a footprint's base_y, so each ring spans the map chunk's whole height (sidecar bounds) from 2 m below to 4 m above. Each trail end leaves a gap on the ring where its gate plane crosses it, as wide as the corridor between the trail's side walls (at most the gate width, portal_adaptations.json gates.half_width_m), so no slot opens beside a side wall; a plug body closes the gap while the link is in warp mode.

trails.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE sections 4.3 and 4.6. Trail side walls (containment layer, player only) follow the ribbon edges side_wall_offset_m outward, side_wall_height_m above the edge, from gate plane to gate plane; they reach side_wall_below_m under the edge because the trail flanks are walkable collision steeper than the 38 deg floor angle, so a player who got under a wall would slide off the island. A trail zone (RegionIndex) is the ribbon plus zone_margin_m, within zone_band_m of the centreline height. Until the export carries the centreline, the ribbon is derived from the trail mesh: its top is every face within top_max_slope_deg of level (Iteration One builds the top at 36 deg at most and the flanks at 49.6 deg or steeper).

region_invariant.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.3: ten times a second the player's last ground point must lie in current_map, a trail touching it, or the map of an armed gate. Five failing samples in a row push_error the position (dev and test builds fail on it; the traversal bot counts it); release builds also recover to SafeGround.

fall_recovery.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.6: an airborne player below kill_y (the lowest walkable height of the map minus 6 m; the sidecar's own kill_y when the exporter provides one) returns to the last SafeGround point with no damage, matching classic's lack of fall damage. A sea-level kill plane catches anything that leaves every map.

across_counter.reason: Shopkeepers serve across their counter, as in classic (Test G: buy and sell). Pan (16), Sid (20) and Lucy (21), the three MeowDB shop NPCs of Maple Island (canonical shops/*.json npc_id), stand behind counters: a player pressed against the counter front stands 1.90, 2.10 and 1.90 m from them horizontally, and they stand 0.45, 0.45 and 0.8 m above the shop floor. With the default 1.6 m sphere that body was 0.00, 0.20 and 0.04 m outside the zone (playtest probe 2026-10-04), so Sid and Lucy could not be talked to on foot and Pan only with no margin. A 2.4 m sphere, still centred 0.8 m above the NPC's feet, takes in a player standing anywhere along the middle of the counter front, and one pressed against it in front of the keeper is 0.83 (Pan), 0.61 (Sid) and 0.79 m (Lucy) inside (the npcs playtest scenario checks at least 0.4 m, 2026-10-04). Each keeper is the only NPC of his or her shop, so the larger zone cannot take the prompt from another NPC.

npc.reason: MeowDB documents no talk range (classic NPCs are clicked). The interact key talks to a current-map NPC whose talk zone overlaps the player's body: a sphere of 1.6 m (a little more than the 1.5 m body height) centred 0.8 m above the NPC's feet, so the player has to walk up to the NPC. talk_zones lists NPCs whose zone differs, each profile with its own reason (WorldTuning.talk_zone). NPCs placed where a player cannot stand are fixed in the source world, not with a larger zone (docs/runtime/blender_export.md, round 4). Until the Blender export had markers for every MeowDB NPC (MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 3.3: Todd, Sam, Mai), a missing one stood next to player_spawns[0], 2.5 m apart along the map frame, with a warning; the runtime keeps that fallback for future content.

session.reason: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.9 step 4: a save naming an unknown map loads at 000000001 player_spawns[0] (the inferred start map, data/misostory/new_character.json). The saved location's resume point is refreshed from SafeGround four times a second so a save always carries a recent safe position.

environment.reason: Blender's sun strength (index.json environment, W/m^2) has no exact Godot equivalent; the Phase 1 probe matched the Blender look with energy = strength / pi (docs/runtime/blender_export.md, known issue 9). Per-map presets come from data/misostory/maps/<id>.json environment_preset; none differ yet.
